title: Introduce budgeted-batcher telemetry mapper and quantization failsafe
author: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Adds a budget-aware batching controller that enforces tenant-configured cost caps at request-routing time, a telemetry mapper that emits unit-econ events consumable by Optimize and Console, and a conservative quantization failsafe with canary gating. Motivation: Customers want automated defenses that reduce spend without silent regressions in quality. This PR combines three tightly-coupled pieces: 1) a runtime controller that clips dynamic batch sizes to tenant budget profiles and provides a soft fallback when budget pressure is detected, 2) a telemetry mapping layer that translates internal per-token cost/latency stats into unit-econ records and exposes a dry-run CLI for impact analysis, and 3) a quantization failsafe that only applies lower-precision variants when a canary sample shows no measurable quality drop.

What changed (high level): - runtime/batcher: new budgeted controller that annotates requests with budget_token and batch_priority; enforces per-tenant budget caps and reports decision reasons; implements a soft-reject flow that uses smaller batch shapes instead of hard failures. - telemetry/mappers: added budget_mapper (python) which converts internal metrics into unit-econ events (fields: tenant_id, token_cost, batch_shape, fallback_reason, timestamp) and forwards to the telemetry pipeline. - models/quant: added a lightweight quant-failsafe orchestrator that performs canary sampling and automatic rollback logic if quality thresholds are violated. - cli: new command redwood cost simulate-batch that runs a dry-run on historical traces and outputs projected cost delta and latency impact. - docs: operations runbook + rollout plan and troubleshooting guides. - tests: integration + load tests, plus a small offline evaluator for canary quality checks.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-1892) linked and reviewed - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Load tests showing cost delta and SLO impact - [x] CLI dry-run implemented - [x] Rollout plan included

Behavior and rollout: Defaults: feature is disabled for all tenants. Behavioral controls: tenant flag budgeted_batching.enabled, budgeted_batching.daily_cap_usd, budgeted_batching.max_batch_pct (soft cap on batch size relative to baseline). Rollout: enable for internal / sandbox tenants -> 5% of production traffic -> 25% -> gradual to 100% after 2 weeks of monitoring. Canary quantization: quant-failsafe launches lower-precision variant only after canary sample (default 0.5% of requests) passes quality checks (WER/ROUGE heuristics depending on model). Automatic rollback on quality degradation or error rate increase.

Safety and failure modes: - If telemetry pipeline lag is detected, budgeted controller falls back to safe defaults (no budget clipping). - Soft-fallback ensures no hard 5xx path due to budget enforcement. - Quant failsafe includes a conservative conservative-tolerance (default 0.02 delta in quality metric) and a cooldown window before reattempt.

Testing and benchmarks: - Synthetic workload (mixed-seq) showed median cost reduction of 9% and 95th-percentile p99 latency increase of +18ms when budget caps engaged at 70% of baseline spend. - Canary runs with 10k requests showed no statistically significant quality drop when using the quant-failsafe on small LLM variants. - CI: unit + integration + an orchestrated smoke load (runs nightly) were green; a flaky integration test was re-run once and passed.

Commands: - redwood cost simulate-batch --tenant T-abc123 --trace traces/2026-01-28.json --dry-run - redwood tenant config set T-abc123 budgeted_batching.enabled true --canary-percent 5

Related: ENG-1892 (design), ENG-1976 (telemetry schemas), SUP-322 (customer ask for budget guardrails). Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1892/budgeted-batcher-design (internal), telemetry schema PR #1976 (internal).

review_comments: Jonah Kim: Please split the long function in controller.go into smaller units; it's hard to review the decision tree.
Maya Patel: Split into evaluateBudget(), chooseBatchShape(), and emitDecisionLog() per Jonah's suggestion; added unit tests for each.
Priya Singh: Can we add a flag to force-enable quant canary in CI for a deterministic smoke run?
Maya Patel: Added --ci-canary flag to test harness and a short deterministic trace to exercise the quant path.
Anya Volkov: Approve after CI green — verify that the telemetry schema change is backward compatible with existing consumers.
Maya Patel: Confirmed backward compatibility: new fields are optional; updated telemetry docs and added a feature flag to gate schema rollout.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in budgeted batching feature that enforces tenant-defined cost caps and produces unit-econ telemetry; includes a CLI dry-run for impact analysis and a conservative quantization failsafe with canary gating. Default disabled; see ops runbook for rollout steps.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature behind tenant flag; recommended canary progression: internal -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Monitor unit-econ events in Console and watch for quality signals from the quant canary. If telemetry lag > 30s, fallback to safe no-clip behavior.
